items.followUp: What is phishing, and how can a user avoid it?

rubric.why: Identifies the advance payment that characterizes this scam.
rubric.description: States that the victim is asked to pay a fee before receiving a benefit.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning an upfront or advance fee.

rubric.why: Shows that the promised benefit is part of a deceptive scheme.
rubric.description: States that a benefit is promised but not delivered, or that the fraudster keeps the fee.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the false promise or explaining that the victim's fee is kept.

modelAnswer: Advance fee fraud is a scam in which a victim is asked to pay an upfront fee to receive a promised reward, loan, or large sum of money.
The promised benefit is not delivered, and the fraudster keeps the fee.

items.followUp: What is plagiarism, and why is it considered unethical?

rubric.why: Explains the protective purpose of copyright law.
rubric.description: States that copyright law legally protects creators or their original work.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning legal protection of original work.

rubric.why: Identifies the control copyright law gives creators over their work.
rubric.description: States that creators can control copying, distribution, or use of their work.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning a form of use over which creators have control.

modelAnswer: Copyright law is the law that gives creators legal protection for their original work.
It gives them control over how their work is copied, distributed, or used.

items.followUp: Name two types of transmission media used in computer networks.

rubric.why: States the main function of a transmission medium.
rubric.description: Explains that it carries or transmits data or signals.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it carries or transmits information.

rubric.why: Identifies the route or endpoints for the communication.
rubric.description: States that data travels between devices or that the medium provides a communication path.
rubric.how: Award for referring to communication between devices or a path for communication.

modelAnswer: A transmission medium is used to carry data or signals from one device to another.
It provides the communication path between devices in a network.

items.followUp: Which HTML tags are used to create a table row and a table cell?

rubric.why: Explains the purpose of making a table in HTML.
rubric.description: States that an HTML table arranges or organizes information in a structured form.
rubric.how: Award for describing the structured organization of information.

rubric.why: Identifies the basic arrangement of information in a table.
rubric.description: States that table information is arranged in rows and columns.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning both rows and columns.

modelAnswer: Making a table in HTML means arranging information in a structured form using HTML table elements.
The information is organized into rows and columns.

items.followUp: What is a website, and how is it different from a web page?

rubric.why: Identifies what a web page is and where it is available.
rubric.description: Defines a web page as a document available on the World Wide Web.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a web document or stating that it is available on the World Wide Web.

rubric.why: Describes how a web page can be accessed.
rubric.description: States that a web page can be viewed using a browser or accessed through its URL.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning a browser or URL.

modelAnswer: A web page is a document available on the World Wide Web.
It can be viewed using a web browser, usually by entering its URL.
